First I'd heard of this, and I play Skullgirls. Is it just Cere?

I feel frustrated, personally. But... it IS a crazy small change. Not nearly as in your face as the HUD change in Path of Exile, say.

I think someone just changed their mind about one bit of design on one single character. What frustrates me the most is that they didn't even mention it, and we all know that they knew damn well what one single little change like this can lead to a lot of suspicion of pandering if it's not discussed by the team, or someone at least saying "hey, we got to thinking, and we decided we like that a little less than we thought we would, so we changed it to something we like more." And, like someone said over at v/GamerGate on the same discussion, as long as they don't try to stop modders from changing those 20 or so frames back to the way they were, there's no reason to get mad about their decision to slightly alter some artistic choices they made. If they try to stop modders from changing that back, we should all probably have cause to worry, though...

I didn't really care very much about the changes as they are so small compared to other games that have censored their artwork (such as the POE HUD change mentioned by /u/Guyven that replaced health and mana babe with a incredibly ugly skull and lion)

However them trying to sweep it under the rug in the patchnotes and then when caught saying that the "changes aren't up for discussion" makes me fucking livid. Enough to make me reconsider buying anything from them ever again.

Well, whether or not they think the change is up for discussion, it'll be up for discussion, so that part I'm not worried about. Whether or not they like it, if their whole audience demands something, they need to deliver or get replaced by someone who does deliver. Their attitude is neither here nor there for me in the equation, but I understand where you're coming from.

you know the argument that it's only 20 frames out of 15k cuts both ways. On the one hand it's no big deal because It's such a small number, on the other hand? It WAS no big deal because it was such a small number. In other words 20 frames out of 15k were changed but because they were such a small number, did they really need to be?

That said this article really does bring up an unusual case of whether or not the action in question can be classified as censorship. with such a minor change that lasts for like a split second every time that frame pops up, yet given the nature of the change it's really hard for me to call it censorship.

The final verdict for me is that I'm not sure if it is classified as censorship given the small impact visually to the game, but given that sex appeal is part of the game's charm, I do not support the change. No longer the case, the more I dwelled on it the more I believe it is, self censorship, but censorship none the less. One thing is certain though, The devs have shown blinding arrogance in saying out right that they will not discuss the change. and ultimately that will hurt more than the actual change. both this game and indivisible.

EDIT: revised opinion.

The best way I can take his remarks are an attempt at disclosure without giving an impression of entertaining feedback on it. That's one thing when you're talking about trying to balance a character's hitbox, and even then saying your player's opinions don't matter is a strangely dictative approach. But we're talking about the art, which is even less the player's concern normally (its not gameplay, its not anything other than correcting a line), BUT this is more than that. Its erasing a panty-shot. Its not 'oops, her leg looks weird in this frame' or 'porportions got off during that move' its... "panties shouldn't be seen 'incidentally'" which IS censorship. That's making a moral call and imposing it on the rest of us. Something like that being "not open to discussion" is troubling, and hurts their reputation more than much anything else they could have changed.

And as you mention, they've got a new game trying to get funded. I hope you don't like what you see of the art they're showing, cause they might decide that bra-straps can't be "incidental" next and change some of it.

I'm still unsure about it being full blown censorship but I still stick to my original thought process and say that not only was it uneccesary, both because the original shots had no real impact on real life, but also because It was completely arbitrary. This was edited well after the games launch. Hell It's not like I disagree wholly with the camp that says it is censorship. They have a well constructed case. But it is hard for me to consider it as full blown censorship. Especially after the genuine case that was hatred being unceremoniously being removed from steam greenlight, and the ESRB's actions during hot coffee controversy.

I've also stated that them saying that them not addressing it and discussing the issue is the most damaging part of this controversy, so your point on that is just parroting. and finally I do like actually like the artstyle of Indivisible, however that games more conservative (?) philosophy regarding the art style has no place in a game like skull girls which was founded on the exact opposite character design philosophy. In other words, Individual IPs can have their own design philosophy going foward, but do not retroactively shoe horn it in to older games and series. If a series was supposed to be all tits all the time cool have at it. If a game want's to have a scaled back low fantasy style with more realistically proportioned characters, great. Just don't try to shoe horn it into the former series if you like the latter's philosophy more and vice versa.
